summary_html: Cases arising on **federal lands/facilities** or involving **Indian children** invoke federal/tribal jurisdictional rules (VICAA for federal facilities; **ICWA** for Indian children and tribal preference/jurisdiction).
authority_html:
- **VICAA (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — federal-facility reporting mandates  
- **ICWA (25 U.S.C. §§ 1901–1963)** — tribal jurisdiction, placement preferences, notice to tribes

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that ICWA's 'active efforts' standard is heightened and more demanding than 'reasonable efforts,' requiring affirmative, active, thorough and timely remedial services tailored to the case, though the agency retains discretion to prioritize services, and it overruled People ex rel. K.D. to the extent inconsistent.
key_cases.relevance: This is the controlling Colorado authority on what ICWA requires of a county department once a child is identified as an Indian child.
key_cases.quote: the active efforts standard under ICWA is a more demanding standard than the reasonable efforts standard applied in non-ICWA cases.

key_cases.holding: The division held that 25 U.S.C. § 1912(f) requires a beyond-a-reasonable-doubt determination of likely serious emotional or physical damage supported by qualified expert testimony, but that the expert need not recite the statutory language, and affirmed the termination.
key_cases.relevance: This decision fixes the qualified-expert-witness requirement that attaches once a case is identified as involving an Indian child.
key_cases.quote: the trial court's determination must be supported by evidence that includes testimony from qualified expert witnesses.

key_cases.holding: The division held that section 19-1-126(1)(a) required the department to make new ICWA inquiries in this case, and that findings and orders from a sibling's earlier case could not alone support a determination that ICWA did not apply; the judgment was reversed and the case remanded.
key_cases.relevance: This is the Colorado authority on the continuing duty of inquiry that triggers ICWA at the front end of every new case, even for a sibling of a child already screened.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that the findings and orders from the prior case alone are insufficient to support the trial court's conclusion that ICWA does not apply in this case.

mandatory_reporters: Enumerated professionals only — Colorado is not a universal-reporter state — Colo. Rev. Stat. § 19-3-304(2) (C.R.S. 2024); any other person may report voluntarily under § 19-3-304(3)
Physicians and surgeons, including physicians in training
Registered nurses and licensed practical nurses
Hospital personnel engaged in the admission, care, or treatment of patients
Public or private school officials and employees
Social workers and workers in any facility or agency licensed or certified by the state
Commercial film and photographic print processors
Clergy members (not for information learned in a communication privileged under Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-90-107(1)(c))
Workers in the state department of human services
Officers and agents of the state bureau of animal protection, and animal control officers
Educators providing services through the federal WIC program
Directors, coaches, assistant coaches, and athletic program personnel employed by a private sports organization or program
Registered psychologist, marriage and family therapist, and licensed professional counselor candidates
Officials and employees of a county department of health or of human or social services
Employees of the department of early childhood
